forecaster_note: Mix of modest S and E swell will give us some chest high surf at the south exposures, more like waist high elsewhere. Clean for most all day with breezy WNW to NW'lies — only the south corners picking up a bit more chop at times. Thursday the same mix continues, waist high at the S magnets, with offshores not as strong as previously forecast and more manageable. Friday brings mixed long and shorter period SSE swell with head sets at the better exposed breaks before NNE winds arrive around midday. — Surfline Sydney Regional Forecast

wind.summary: NW 18 km/h gusting 42 at 9am — offshore all day but genuinely breezy. Eases to W 15 km/h by 3pm, which is the smoothest part of the day. Nothing onshore at any point.

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW live: no shark detections or drone sightings at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly in the last 24 h. Most recent Northern Beaches activity was drone sightings at Bungan Beach (3:00pm) and North Palm Beach (1:58pm) on 31 Aug — about 39 h ago and well north of your spots. Feed is healthy: 8 real statewide detections in the last 24 h, the latest a tagged shark at Lighthouse Beach, Ballina at 6:50pm yesterday.

days.label: Today
days.note: Clean but weak. Energy tops out at 79 kJ — one of the softest days in weeks — and the primary is 2.5ft @ 10s from 178°, dead south, which is exactly the direction that wraps badly into Dee Why. That is the whole story: Long Reef and Curl Curl convert it and sit 3–4ft, Dee Why and Manly get the leftovers at 1–3ft. Consistency is 100/100 so the sets do keep coming, they are just small. Wind is offshore NW all day but gusting 42 km/h at 9am, so it will be putting a bit of chop back into the face. Tide pushes to a 1.56m high at 11:29am — your usual 10am–12pm window lines up well with it. Go to Long Reef or Curl Curl, not the Point.

dee-why.window: 10am–12pm on the tide push if you go at all — but this is the weakest of your four options today. Only worth it if you want a mellow longboard-style paddle.
alerts: 178° is dead south — the worst angle for Dee Why, the bay shadows it
79 kJ is very low energy; expect soft, gutless walls

tip.label: Skip the Point today
tip.text: That 1.6ft @ 10s from 75° is right in your 30–80° sweet spot and would be the wave you want — it is just too small to carry a session on its own. The 2.5ft primary at 178° is textbook dead-south and the headland eats it before it reaches the Point, so you would be paddling for knee-to-waist rollers with 42 km/h of gusty NW on them. Drive the extra five minutes to Curl Curl or Long Reef instead.

long-reef.window: 9am–12pm. Fair on Surfline all day and the biggest of the four — the tide filling to 11:29am helps the banks.
alerts: Best size on the coast today, but only 79 kJ behind it — sizey without punch
NW gusts to 42 km/h at 9am will feather the tops

tip.label: The pick of a small day
tip.text: Long Reef faces straight into the 178° primary, which is precisely why it doubles Dee Why's size on the same swell. Waist-to-shoulder at Fair with 100/100 consistency is a real session — plenty of waves, just no power in them. Straight-hand rights off the reef end put you frontside. Go on the smallest, most volume-forward board you own; today is a paddle-count day, not a power day.

curl-curl.window: 9am–12pm while it holds Fair. North Curly corner for the cleanest shape out of the NW gusts.
alerts: Drops toward Poor–Fair after midday as the swell trims back
Mixed 178° S and 29° NNE means crossed-up peaks — banks will be shifty

tip.label: Closest thing to shape today
tip.text: Curly is the S-swell magnet of the four, so it converts more of the 178° than Dee Why without the paddle of Long Reef. The catch is the 2.4ft @ 6s NNE windswell sitting almost on top of the S — crossed-up peaks that wall and then back off. North Curly corner tidies that up and gets some shelter from the NW. Sit wide, pick the ones with a bit of S in them and let the short-period lumps go through.

manly.window: Not worth a special trip. If you are already in Manly, 10am–12pm on the tide push at North Steyne.
alerts: Most sheltered of the four from a 178° swell — smallest waves today

tip.label: The default no
tip.text: North Steyne needs east in the swell to fire and today's usable east component is only 1.6ft @ 10s. With the S primary shadowed by the Corso end and just 79 kJ overall, this is a knee-to-waist day. Fine for a coffee-and-a-splash, wrong call for your mid-morning window.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Same mix, a notch smaller and cleaner. The S primary swings to 172° @ 12s — longer period, so slightly more organised — but drops to 2.1ft, and a 2.5ft @ 5s NNE windswell sits over the top. Energy still 79 kJ, consistency still 100/100. Surfline has the offshores easing from earlier forecasts, so it should be more manageable than today: NNW 10 km/h at dawn building to W 22 km/h by 3pm. Long Reef and Curl Curl are Fair through the morning and slide off after midday. Dawn to 11am is the whole session.

dee-why.window: Nothing here worth the drive. 6–9am if you want a clean paddle before work.
alerts: 172° still too far south for the Point to switch on

long-reef.window: 6–11am while it holds Fair. Drops to Poor–Fair from 3pm.
alerts: Smaller than today — the S primary trims to 2.1ft

curl-curl.window: 6–11am. Rated Poor by 3pm, so this is a strictly-morning day.
alerts: Steepest drop-off of the four — Fair at 9am, Poor by 3pm

manly.window: Skip it. Smallest of the four again.
alerts: 1–2ft all day, Poor–Fair from dawn to dark

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Circle Sunday afternoon. Saturday is the throwaway — 1–3ft, energy down to 55 kJ, consistency slipping to 77%, and a W/WNW offshore that builds to 32 km/h gusting 64 by evening. Then Sunday flips hard: a long-period S groundswell lands from around midday, 6.3ft @ 12s from 184°, and energy explodes from 27 kJ at 9am to 846 kJ by 3pm — the biggest number on the chart in weeks. Long Reef goes 2–8ft, Curl Curl 2–6ft, Dee Why 1–5ft. Two catches: 184° is dead south again, so Dee Why will be the shadowed one, and the wind swings ESE onshore 14–17 km/h from midday just as the swell arrives. Monday 7 Sep is the smarter play — 3–4ft holding, 4.7ft @ 10s and consistency back to 97–100%.

dee-why.window: Sat: 6–9am before the W wind gets silly. Sun: 12–3pm as the groundswell fills, accepting ESE onshore texture.
alerts: Sunday's 184° primary is dead south — expect Dee Why to under-perform the raw numbers again
ESE onshore from midday Sunday, exactly when the swell peaks

long-reef.window: Sat: 6–11am, small but clean. Sun: 12–4pm is where the size is — 846 kJ and up to 8ft, a serious step-up session.
alerts: Sunday afternoon is genuinely big — 8ft with 846 kJ behind it, plan the paddle-out
ESE onshore will add bump to sets that are already thick

curl-curl.window: Sat: 6–11am. Sun: 12–3pm at North Curly, sweep will be heavy once 846 kJ arrives.
alerts: Strong sweep expected Sunday afternoon with the S groundswell running
Rated Poor–Fair right through Sunday despite the size — the ESE onshore is the reason

manly.window: Neither day. Most shadowed of the four from a 184° swell.
alerts: Stays 1–3ft even on Sunday's 846 kJ pulse — wrong angle entirely
